title: Scalar extension and cofibrant evaluation for dg modules
statement:
Use small dg categories and quasi-equivalences as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the module Hom complexes of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution], and the projective model structures on dg-module categories of [lem-coef-dg-module-diagram-classification]. For a dg category $\mathcal C$ write $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$ for covariant dg functors $\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$; thus right $\mathcal B$-modules are $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$. All tensor products of dg categories use object pairs, tensor products of morphism complexes over $\mathbf Z$, and the Koszul sign in interchanging homogeneous factors.

For any dg functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, restriction $u^*$ has a left adjoint $u_!$ given by
$$(u_!M)(e)=\int^{c\in\mathcal C}\mathcal E(u(c),e)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}M(c).$$
Here the coend is the quotient of the direct sum over objects $c$ by the two action relations indexed by the morphism complexes of $\mathcal C$, using the graded symmetry when factors are interchanged. This is a Quillen adjunction for the projective model structures: $u_!$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, equivalently $u^*$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Its derived left adjoint is computed by applying $u_!$ to a projectively cofibrant replacement. If $u$ is a quasi-equivalence, this adjunction is a Quillen equivalence: the derived unit and counit are isomorphisms on the localized module categories. The analogous assertions for right modules use $u^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a right representable $h_b=\mathcal B(-,b)$ and $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$, extension on right modules sends $h_b$ canonically to $h_{v(b)}$, and sends cofibrant modules to cofibrant modules and weak equivalences between cofibrant modules to weak equivalences. Scalar extensions have their canonical unital associative isomorphisms $(vu)_!\cong v_!u_!$, satisfying the unit and pentagon identities.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal B$ be small dg categories and assume each $\mathcal C(c,c')$ is projectively cofibrant as a complex. Evaluation at any $c$ from $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$ to right $\mathcal B$-modules sends projectively cofibrant objects to projectively cofibrant objects. Equivalently, a projectively cofibrant diagram of right $\mathcal B$-modules indexed by such a $\mathcal C$ has cofibrant values.

A complex is homotopically flat if tensoring it with any quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism. If $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ is a quasi-equivalence and both categories have homotopically flat morphism complexes, then $u\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ is a quasi-equivalence for every small dg category $\mathcal D$, with no flatness assumption on $\mathcal D$. Consequently restriction along this tensor functor induces an equivalence of localized module categories, with inverse its derived extension of scalars. In particular this applies when $\mathcal C,\mathcal E$ are cofibrant dg categories.

source.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.2 (complexes as coefficient model category), Proposition 3.3 and Corollary 3.4; Section 4, tensor product and derived tensor product paragraphs before Definition 4.1. For the homotopically flat formulation compare Keller, On differential graded categories, Section 4.2, the definition of k-flat and rep(A,B) before Theorem 4.2; the tensor argument uses K-flat complexes. Coend adjunction and its unit/associativity are the scalar-extension construction in Section 3. Read online; absent locally. No Stacks tag supplies these dg-module assertions.

proof.text:
Construct the displayed coend degreewise as a quotient complex. Its relations are
$$[f\,u(a)\otimes m]=[f\otimes M(a)m],\qquad a\in\mathcal C(c,c'),\ f\in\mathcal E(u(c'),e),\ m\in M(c),$$
for homogeneous elements; the tensor order here is $f\otimes a\otimes m$, so no interchange sign is suppressed. The two maps imposing these relations are chain maps, because the actions and composition are chain maps. Postcomposition in $\mathcal E$ gives the covariant action on this quotient. Complexes have the required coproducts and quotients by [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. For a module chain map $t:M\to u^*N$ define $\overline t_e([f\otimes m])=N(f)t_c(m)$. Its balancing equation is precisely the displayed relation and naturality of $t$. Conversely send $s:u_!M\to N$ to $t_c(m)=s_{u(c)}([1_{u(c)}\otimes m])$. The unit and the balancing relation show that the two constructions are inverse, and their formulas commute with maps of $M,N$. This proves the ordinary adjunction and its specified coend formula; no existence theorem for enriched Kan extensions is being used without its construction.

source.place: Section 3, scalar extension before Proposition 3.2; Proposition 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Corollary 3.4; Section 4, tensor products before Definition 4.1. Explicit module and K-flat arguments supplied by the worker.

proof.text:
Use the unital associative dg composition of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] and the representable right modules, with action by composition, defined in [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement]. Write $r^c=\mathcal C(c,-)$. The map
$$u_!r^c(e)\longrightarrow\mathcal E(u(c),e),\qquad [f\otimes a]\longmapsto f\,u(a)$$
has inverse $z\mapsto[z\otimes1_c]$; balancing proves both inverse equations. For right modules, apply the displayed coend formula to $v^{\mathrm{op}}$: it gives $v_!h_b\cong h_{v(b)}$. In the order used in step 1, this right-module map sends $[f\otimes a]$ with $f\in\mathcal E(e,v(x))$, $a\in\mathcal B(x,b)$ to $(-1)^{|f||a|}v(a)f$, the composition in the opposite dg category. Its inverse is again $z\mapsto[z\otimes1_b]$. For composable $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, $v:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, the comparison $v_!u_!M\to(vu)_!M$ sends $[g\otimes[f\otimes m]]$ to $[g\,v(f)\otimes m]$. Its inverse sends $[h\otimes m]$ to $[h\otimes[1_{u(c)}\otimes m]]$. Each relation on either side is taken to a balancing relation on the other; the two composites reduce to the identity by balancing. For the identity functor the unitor is $[f\otimes m]\mapsto M(f)m$. On any iterated pure tensor, every path in a unit or pentagon diagram is the same ordered composite of morphisms applied to $m$; associativity and the unit law in the dg categories give equality. Pure tensors generate the quotient, proving the canonical coherences.

proof.text: The projective module models exist by [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] with coefficient model $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$. Restriction retains selected object values, so it preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations, which are respectively objectwise surjections and objectwise surjective quasi-isomorphisms. In an adjunction a lifting problem against $u_!i$ is exactly a lifting problem against $i$ and $u^*p$; hence the left lifting definitions show that $u_!$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It preserves the initial module, and therefore cofibrant modules. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to these two complete and cocomplete model categories and this adjunction. It gives the derived adjunction, computed on a projectively cofibrant replacement on the left; restriction preserves every objectwise quasi-isomorphism, so its derived functor is restriction itself. The same cited statement gives preservation by $u_!$ of weak equivalences between cofibrant modules. All these assertions apply to opposites as well.

proof.text: Suppose $u$ is a quasi-equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ to obtain, for every covariant module $M$, a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to M$ with a graded-split filtration whose successive quotients are sums of shifts of representables. The semi-free cell-presentation and cofibrancy assertion [lem-coef-dg-semi-free-cofibrant] applies to this $P$.

proof.text: Give $u_!P$ the filtration $u_!P_i$. Forgetting differentials, each $P_i\subset P_{i+1}$ is a split sum of graded modules. The graded coend is additive and preserves direct sums and quotients by its explicit direct-sum quotient formula (step 1), so these remain split inclusions with quotient $u_!(P_{i+1}/P_i)$, and their union is $u_!P$. Restriction is objectwise, so the target filtration of $\eta_P:P\to u^*u_!P$ is also graded-split and exhaustive. On each quotient, the representable computation of step 2 identifies the unit with sums of shifts of $\mathcal C(c,x)\to\mathcal E(u(c),u(x))$. Each is a quasi-isomorphism by the hypothesis on $u$. A cycle in a direct sum has finite support, so taking primitives in those finitely many summands proves that direct sums preserve these quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dg-filtered-quasi-iso] objectwise to the unit with the two exhaustive graded-split filtrations of step 5, starting at zero. Its successive quotient maps are quasi-isomorphisms by that step, so $\eta_P$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: For an arbitrary cofibrant $M$, both $P$ and $M$ are cofibrant, and [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] makes $u_!q$ a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of $\eta$ and two-out-of-three then make $\eta_M$ a quasi-isomorphism. For a general $M$, the replacement $QM\to M$ now proves that its derived unit is invertible.

proof.text:
Restriction detects objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of $\mathcal E$-modules when $u$ is a quasi-equivalence. Indeed for every $e$ choose an isomorphism $u(c)\cong e$ in $H^0\mathcal E$, represented by closed degree-zero arrows $a,b$ with $ba-1=dh$, $ab-1=dk$. Applying any dg module carries these equations to chain homotopies: for example $N(b)N(a)-1=dN(h)+N(h)d$. Thus a natural map of modules is a quasi-isomorphism at $e$ if it is so at $u(c)$, by the naturality square with these homotopy equivalences. For $N$ choose $q:Q(u^*N)\to u^*N$. The derived counit is the ordinary-adjoint transpose $\epsilon:u_!Q(u^*N)\to N$. Its restriction satisfies
$$u^*\epsilon\circ\eta_{Q(u^*N)}=q.$$
The unit is a quasi-isomorphism by steps 4–7, so $u^*\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and detection makes $\epsilon$ one too. The derived adjunction of step 3 therefore has invertible unit and counit. This proves the asserted Quillen equivalence without imposing local cofibrancy on $\mathcal C$ or $\mathcal E$.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] first with coefficient model $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ and index $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. It says that $\mathcal N$ is complete, cocomplete, locally presentable, enriched, tensored and cotensored, satisfies the enriched model axiom and the tensor-cell acyclicity condition, has all objects fibrant, and has generating cofibrations between cofibrant objects. It therefore satisfies every hypothesis for a second application of that node with index $\mathcal C$. Its evaluation clause applies because each $\mathcal C(c,c')$ is projectively cofibrant, and gives cofibrant values of projectively cofibrant $\mathcal C$-diagrams. Write $A(a)$ for the degree-$|a|$ action of $a\in\mathcal C(c,c')$ and $B(\beta)$ for that of $\beta\in\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}(b,b')$. The enriched naturality equation from the cited node is $B(\beta)A(a)=(-1)^{|a||\beta|}A(a)B(\beta)$. Set $T(a\otimes\beta)=A(a)B(\beta)$ on the complexes $T(c,b)$. For composable homogeneous pairs, the composite of these operators is $(-1)^{|\beta'||a|}A(a'a)B(\beta'\beta)$, exactly the tensor-category composition. The differential rule follows from the Leibniz rule for the two actions. Conversely restrict a tensor-category action to $a\otimes1_b$ and $1_c\otimes\beta$; their two composites give this same signed equation and recover the original action on $a\otimes\beta$. Degree-zero chain maps commute with the tensor action exactly when they commute with both restricted actions. These inverse constructions give the currying identification $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}\cong\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$. Objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations agree in the two descriptions, so their left lifting classes, hence projectively cofibrant objects, agree. This proves the evaluation assertion, with no hypothesis on the Hom complexes of $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Section 3, scalar extension before Proposition 3.2; Proposition 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Corollary 3.4; Section 4, tensor products before Definition 4.1. Explicit module and K-flat arguments supplied by the worker.

proof.text:
Here is the complex argument needed for the final tensor assertion. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] to the one-object dg category with endomorphisms $\mathbf Z[0]$. It gives every complex $V$ a quasi-isomorphism $P\to V$, where $P$ has a graded-split increasing filtration with quotients sums of shifts of $\mathbf Z$. For any acyclic complex $A$, the tensor filtration of $P\otimes A$ is still graded-split and its quotients are sums of shifts of $A$, hence acyclic. In a direct sum a cycle has finite support; choose a primitive in each of those finitely many summands to see this last assertion directly. Apply [lem-coef-dg-filtered-quasi-iso] to $0\to P\otimes A$ with its zero source filtration and this exhaustive graded-split target filtration: the quotient maps are quasi-isomorphisms because their targets are acyclic. Thus $P\otimes A$ is acyclic. Tensor commutes with the direct-sum cone: for $f:X\to Y$ put $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ with $d(y,x)=(dy+f(x),-dx)$. The total tensor differential identifies $\operatorname{Cone}(f)\otimes P$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(f\otimes1_P)$. It follows that $P$ is homotopically flat.

If $K$ is both acyclic and homotopically flat, then $K\otimes V$ is acyclic for every $V$: for the replacement $P\to V$ just constructed, $K\otimes P\to K\otimes V$ is a quasi-isomorphism by flatness of $K$, while $K\otimes P$ is acyclic by flatness of $P$ applied to $K\to0$. Finally, the cone of a map between homotopically flat complexes is homotopically flat. For an acyclic $A$, its tensor with that cone is the cone between two acyclic complexes, hence acyclic by the same cycle calculation. Applied to the cone of an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism, this is precisely the defining flatness test. This argument requires no flatness of $V$.

proof.text: For every pair $c,c'$ the local map $f:\mathcal C(c,c')\to\mathcal E(u(c),u(c'))$ is a quasi-isomorphism between homotopically flat complexes. By step 10 its cone is acyclic and homotopically flat, so its tensor with $\mathcal D(d,d')$ is acyclic even when that latter complex is not flat. The cone-tensor identity there says exactly that $f\otimes1_{\mathcal D(d,d')}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $u\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ is locally a quasi-isomorphism. For an object $(e,d)$ choose the closed degree-zero arrows $a:u(c)\to e$, $b:e\to u(c)$ from essential surjectivity. The arrows $a\otimes1_d$, $b\otimes1_d$ are inverse in $H^0$ because the boundaries $dh$, $dk$ become $d(h\otimes1_d)$, $d(k\otimes1_d)$. This proves essential surjectivity and hence quasi-equivalence. Steps 3–8 applied to this dg functor give the asserted localized module equivalence with inverse derived extension. Finally [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] explicitly states that the Hom complexes of a cofibrant dg category are projectively cofibrant and homotopically flat, so cofibrant $\mathcal C,\mathcal E$ meet the hypotheses. Empty source or tensor categories cause no exception: a quasi-equivalence from an empty category has empty target, and the module category of an empty category has its single empty diagram.
